glossary.title: Stat & Rule Glossary
glossary.help: Definitions for all metrics, rules, and analytical concepts used in the Madness Index.

entries.definition: A composite rating that summarizes a team’s tournament identity using baseline strength and profile breadth. MI is designed to be stable, comparable across teams, and readable as a single-number anchor.
A running record of evaluated matchups, capturing the teams, round context, and the system’s outputs at the time of analysis. It functions as an audit trail for recent comparisons.
An alternate evaluation state that allows manual adjustments without treating the result as an official matchup outcome. It is used for testing inputs, edge cases, and “what-if” scenarios.

The identity-only foundation of MI built from baseline strength plus breadth, without any résumé points being added into the baseline. It represents a team’s underlying profile before matchup interaction scaling.

A baseline add-on that rewards teams with wider, more reliable profile coverage across core traits. It reflects how many different ways a team can sustain performance without relying on one narrow strength.
The matchup-adjusted version of MI after interaction metrics are applied between the two teams. It represents how each profile scales when placed directly against the opponent.
The net separation between the two teams’ matchup outputs, expressed as a single gap value. MI Δ is the primary “distance” signal used to summarize how far apart the profiles evaluate.

A set of directional indicators derived from the interaction layer that summarize where the matchup pressure is coming from. Lean Signals describe the type of edge being created, not a guaranteed result.
A possession-based measure of how efficiently a team converts offense into points. OffEff describes scoring output per trip, independent of pace.
A possession-based measure of how efficiently a team prevents scoring. DefEff describes points allowed per opponent trip, independent of pace.
The net efficiency gap between a team’s offense and defense on a per-possession basis. EM summarizes overall strength by combining both sides of the ball into one differential.
A scoring efficiency rate that accounts for two-point shots, three-point shots, and free throws in one percentage. TS% represents overall point conversion efficiency per shot attempt.

A shooting efficiency rate that adjusts field-goal percentage to account for the added value of three-point shots. eFG% reflects how efficiently a team converts shot attempts into points from the field.
The opponent shooting efficiency a team allows, adjusted for the added value of three-point shots. Def eFG% reflects how well a defense limits quality shot conversion.
A possession-quality indicator that summarizes how reliably a team turns trips into usable scoring chances. EPR reflects possession management beyond raw pace or shooting splits.
The share of possessions that end in a turnover rather than a shot attempt or trip to the line. TO% reflects ball security and offensive stability.
The statistical baselines used to normalize team trait values across the full dataset. Mean and standard deviation define what counts as typical, strong, or extreme in each metric.
A classification rule that groups metric values into meaningful bands based on distance from the dataset average. Tiers express how far a team sits from “normal” within a given trait.
A static identity score that measures how strongly a team’s profile supports a Cinderella-style upset narrative. CIS reflects underdog viability as an identity signal, not a prediction.
A static identity score that measures how strongly a team’s profile supports favorite-level stability and control. FAS reflects chalk reliability as an identity signal, not a prediction.
A round-aware identity score that updates Cinderella alignment based on opponent, path, and current round framing. LCI reflects the Cinderella signal in the present matchup context.
A round-aware identity score that updates favorite alignment based on opponent, path, and current round framing. LFI reflects the favorite signal in the present matchup context.

The identity label applied when a matchup does not cleanly resolve into standard Cinderella-versus-favorite framing. It indicates a non-standard identity state such as mirror, neutral, or chaos conditions.

A résumé-strength layer used to describe schedule quality and accomplishment signals alongside the profile model. Résumé Context is separate from baseline MI and is applied only through interaction scaling.
The résumé classification band assigned to a team based on its résumé context strength. Tiers provide a compact summary of résumé quality without describing specific results.
A set of named flags that tag notable profile patterns that can matter in tournament play. Marks are descriptive signals, not standalone ratings or guarantees.
A profile mark indicating a team’s offense is built around a narrow scoring shape or limited scoring pathways. It describes an offense that can be easier to map if its primary option is contained.
A profile mark indicating perimeter outcomes are highly variable or structurally vulnerable within the profile. It flags a team whose outside layer is less reliable or more matchup-sensitive.
A profile mark indicating low or inconsistent three-point shot conversion relative to peer baselines. It describes a profile that does not reliably generate scoring from the arc.
A profile mark indicating a defense that concedes avoidable advantages through fouls, breakdowns, or poor containment. It flags defensive execution risk rather than scheme identity.
A profile mark indicating the interior defense yields efficiency or access near the rim relative to baseline expectations. It describes a profile that can struggle to consistently protect the paint.
A profile mark indicating the defense allows elevated perimeter shot quality or volume compared to baseline. It flags an outside-containment vulnerability rather than shooting variance.
A profile mark indicating performance is less stable when pace rises or possession flow becomes chaotic. It flags a profile that can lose efficiency under speed or disruption.
The set of pressure-based matchup measures that compare two teams’ profiles trait-by-trait. Interaction Metrics translate profile differences into directional competitive friction.
An interaction measure describing how three-point volume, quality, and perimeter defense intersect between the two teams. It captures the matchup’s outside shooting and containment tension.
An interaction measure describing how foul pressure and free-throw dependence intersect between the two teams. It captures the matchup’s line-access and foul-risk tension.
An interaction measure describing how interior scoring leverage meets interior resistance between the two teams. It captures the matchup’s paint efficiency and rim protection tension.
An interaction measure describing how ball security meets turnover forcing between the two teams. It captures the matchup’s control versus disruption tension on possessions.
An interaction measure describing how rebounding and extra-possession generation intersect between the two teams. It captures the matchup’s offensive glass and cleanup leverage.

An interaction measure describing how physical play tolerance intersects with the opponent’s ability to absorb or punish contact. It captures the matchup’s strength-through-contact and foul-resilience tension.

An interaction measure describing how shot selection discipline intersects with the opponent’s ability to restrict preferred attempts. It captures the matchup’s ability to force or avoid low-value shots.
An interaction measure describing how outcome variance intersects with the opponent’s stability profile. It captures the matchup’s swing potential as a profile interaction signal.

formula.card: Each Madness Index score starts from MI_base, a blend of Core Traits, Breadth, and Résumé Context. Matchup-specific interaction leverage is added on top to get MI_matchup.

core.card: Core Traits measure who a team is possession-to-possession: offensive efficiency, defensive efficiency, shooting quality, and possession control.
core.tile: This tile shows each core stat, how it grades versus the 64-team field, and how much weight it carries in the Core composite.

breadth.card: Breadth rewards teams that are strong in multiple core areas at once rather than leaning on a single spike. More overlapping strengths create a larger Breadth bonus.
breadth.tile: The Breadth summary highlights how many core metrics clear the above-average threshold and how much bonus that coverage adds.

resume.card: Résumé Context blends record and schedule strength into a single index. Elite résumés earn a small boost; fragile or inflated résumés receive a stronger skepticism penalty.
resume.tile: This tile summarizes how the team's win percentage and schedule difficulty stack up versus the field and how that converts into a résumé adjustment.

Elite: This résumé reflects substantial success across one of the most demanding schedules in all of college basketball.
It provides strong contextual validation for how this team's profile reads relative to other teams in the field.
Strong: This résumé reflects consistent success against a high-quality level of competition.
It indicates a profile whose strengths hold up well under context rather than relying on favorable game conditions.
Above Average: This résumé presents a record that is supported by a reasonably demanding slate of opponents.
It suggests a profile whose signals are strengthened by the competition it has faced.

It suggests a profile that reads as expected once record and competition are considered together.

It suggests a profile that may look stronger on paper, and may not have been fully clarified by higher-level opposition.
Fragile: This résumé presents modest results and performance combined with limited exposure to stronger competition.
It suggests a profile that becomes increasingly difficult to interpret as competition levels rise.
fallback: This résumé tier reflects how the team’s results and schedule context compare to the tournament field.

marks.card: Profile Marks are diagnostic flags. They do not change the score directly, but they reveal structural strengths or vulnerabilities that may matter in specific matchups.
marks.tile: Each badge reflects a repeatable pattern in the stats (for example, rim softness, turnover fragility, or cold perimeter shooting). Use them as quick scouting shortcuts.

identity.tile: Tournament Identity blends CIS (Cinderella Index Score) and FAS (Favorite Alignment Score) into a single snapshot of how this team tends to show up in a bracket.

phrases.Average: an offense that can hold its own

back_phrases.Elite: This offense reliably turns possessions into high-quality results, flowing into strong chances and finishing them with poise. They maintain pressure throughout the game and are difficult to disrupt without major defensive adjustments.
back_phrases.Strong: Their offense produces steady, repeatable scoring by creating workable looks and converting them at a strong clip. Opponents can slow them in stretches, but they generally find their way back into rhythm.
back_phrases.Above Average: They generate enough clean chances to keep pace against most opponents, especially when spacing and tempo break their way. While not dominant, their scoring can carry stretches when the game opens up.
back_phrases.Average: Their offense is capable but not forceful, relying more on solid execution than natural advantage. They can score within the flow of the game but rarely dictate terms without help from pace or matchups.
back_phrases.Weak: They struggle to create or finish quality looks consistently, leading to long, momentum-halting possessions. When the game tightens, their scoring can fade and leave them searching for answers.
back_phrases.Fragile: This offense often breaks down before good opportunities develop, resulting in extended droughts that opponents can exploit. They seldom find stable scoring rhythm and rely heavily on game script going their way.
